column16: Name in 2002/03 was NK Valpovka - Satnica (renamed NK Valpovka on 7 July 2003, hr.wikipedia NK Valpovka Valpovo); RSSSF lists Valpovka Valpovo. Stadium and founded from hr.wikipedia club page: no second source. Capacity unknown. Home kit all green, colour2 White from second kit; colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)

Row right: season page and RSSSF put the club in the South group 2002/03 (12th, relegated); the EN club page wrongly says they dropped to Treca HNL in 2002/03. RSSSF table name is TSK Naftas Topolovac (sponsor name?). Stadium and capacity are today's ground from the club page; ground used in 2002/03 not confirmed (inference). Š has a Windows-1252 form but the database style strips it. colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)

Founded June 2003, took the place of Omladinac Novo Selo Rok (RSSSF: merger of Omladinac and Sloga Cakovec). North winners 2003/04, promoted via play-off. Đ has no Windows-1252 form, written D. Capacity: transfermarkt gives 6,000 seats. colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)

Renamed NK Valpovka on 7 July 2003 (hr.wikipedia). 11th in North, relegation play-off. Stadium and founded from hr.wikipedia club page: no second source. Capacity unknown. Home kit all green, colour2 White from second kit; colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)

8th in North 2005/06. Č has no Windows-1252 form, written C. Capacity: transfermarkt gives 6,000 seats. Founded from EN and hr.wikipedia club pages. colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)

Capacity: EN season page 2,000, hr.wikipedia club page 500, transfermarkt 0 seats; doubt. Founded unknown. Club merged with NK HASK in July 2006 and folded 2017 (hr.wikipedia). ć has no Windows-1252 form, written c. Š has a Windows-1252 form but the database style strips it. colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)

Division wrong in the database: 2009/10 Druga HNL was one 14-club league with no North group. Promoted as 3. HNL West winners, 7th. Stadium: transfermarkt gives SC Rudes, 2,000 seats (today); stadium and capacity from one source only, doubt. Founded 1957 agrees with Nogometni leksikon (nogomet.lzmk.hr). colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)

Division wrong in the database: 2010/11 Druga HNL was one 16-club league with no North group. Promoted as 3. HNL South winners, 8th. RSSSF kroa2011.html agrees with club and division. Founded: Wikipedia 1952 (as NK Proleter), transfermarkt 30/11/1951. colours from the current kit in the club's Wikipedia infobox (inference for that season)
